summary: Builds Ada, a read-only repository code-understanding agent with a seven-tool interface, and records 408 trajectories (6 repos x 4 task families x 4 models x 4 prompt conditions = 384, plus 24 coach-judge runs on GPT-4.1). Five 'observation lenses' (surface counts, journey arcs, transition grammar, LLM-judge adjudication, repository footprints) characterize model behavior under budget pressure, prior suppression, and external coaching.

claims.claim: Budget pressure compresses exploration (turns, LOC, files, time) for all four models while raising per-turn effort.
claims.evidence: Figures 4-5 (Finding 1); GPT-4.1 time/turn ~5s -> >15s. Authors note wall-clock is confounded with serving latency (Pearson r=0.397 with output length).

claims.claim: Behavioral and judged-quality profiles are mainly model-characteristic; conditions cause smaller shifts.
claims.evidence: Fig. 8: task relevance T1 0.174 (GPT-4o) to 0.868 (Qwen) vs condition range 0.608-0.632; Table 6. One trajectory per grid cell, no repeated runs.

claims.claim: External coach-judge intervention increases activity (2.5x turns, 3.4x files) but lowers conclusion grounding (median ~0.68 vs 0.85-0.95).
claims.evidence: §4.3, 24 trajectories, GPT-4.1 only, DeepSeek-V3 as coach/judges; grounding scored by LLM judges whose human alignment is weakest on Trace Grounding (Appendix 11, Table 15).
RQ2 summary synthesizes lens readings; convergence judged by LLM adjudication only.

patterns.note: Replayable trajectories plus lenses make agent navigation/stopping observable; full replication package.

Three-model judge vote with inter-judge agreement and a 250-item single-annotator human check; termination calibration has weak agreement and judges agree with each other more than with the human on grounding.
Turn-budget pressure cuts exploration without collapsing judged quality but lowers termination calibration (0.715 -> 0.633).
Tool surface is structural overview + code-region peeking; these two account for 80.1% of calls.
Explicitly not benchmark-driven; observation of open-ended tasks.

methodology.sample: 408 trajectories; 6 repos (Requests, Flask, scikit-learn, Graphiti in Python; Prompt Optimizer in TypeScript; TensorZero in Rust); 4 task families.
methodology.baselines: Natural condition as reference; no alternative scaffolds.
methodology.models: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1 (via GitHub Copilot runtime, default temperature), DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (temp 0.2); judges GLM-5, Kimi-K2.5, MiniMax-M2.7; coach DeepSeek-V3.
methodology.variance: One run per grid cell; within-condition variance shown qualitatively; no CIs on judged scores.
methodology.ablations: Prompt-framing conditions act as perturbations; coach condition only on GPT-4.1.
methodology.contamination_controls: Prior-suppression prompt condition; popular repos (Flask, Requests, scikit-learn) are surely in training data.
methodology.languages: Python (4 repos), TypeScript (1), Rust (1); no Java.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; formatted for a Springer venue but no acceptance listed.
standards.artifacts: Zenodo replication package: apparatus code, all 408 trajectories, lens outputs, scripts, judge prompts.

biases.detail: Single trajectory per configuration; model-level differences may include run noise.
Partial validation only: one human annotator on 250 items; weakest agreement on dimensions driving key findings (termination calibration, trace grounding).
Well-known OSS repos; prior-suppression is only a prompt instruction.
Coach-judge finding rests on 24 GPT-4.1 runs.
GPT-4o/GPT-4.1 served through Copilot with uncontrolled decoding.

coi.funding: Not stated; COI declaration says none.
coi.detail: Academic study with no product interest.

verdict_reason: Well-documented, fully released trajectory study across four models and six repos, with honest limitation sections; but one run per cell, read-only code-understanding tasks, partially validated LLM judges, and a small single-model intervention arm limit what can be concluded about harness design.
applicability: Useful for the team's observability practice more than for design choices: recording replayable trajectories and analysing navigation footprints/stopping is a cheap way to compare hosts (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) on the same ingestion repos. The coach-judge result is a caution against injecting an always-on LLM supervisor into the agent loop; deterministic gates are safer. Repos are Python/TS/Rust and tasks are read-only understanding, so nothing here measures Java or multi-repo change work.

conflicts_with.detail: Ada's LLM coach-judge intervention extended runs and lowered judged grounding, whereas SPOQ reports that review/validation interventions reduce defects; different task types, so tension rather than direct contradiction.
